lines.caption: This is a tour of pull request 80, which stops Thunar's file-operation dialogs from stealing the focus.
It has three parts: what this PR adds, how it was built and verified, and what comes later.
Part 1. What this PR adds.
You start a copy in Thunar and go back to typing in another app.
After half a second, the progress window appears without asking for the focus.
When a job needs attention, an open progress window is only un-minimized, never raised, so it can't take the focus.
A job's question or error dialog no longer has a default button for Enter to press.
The dialog opens with its focus on its message text, not on a button.
It is put on screen first, and only then made modal.
You answer by clicking, or by tabbing to a button. Escape still cancels, once you focus the dialog.
Before, the progress window and the replace dialog took your keyboard, and a stray Enter could cancel the copy.
Window managers focus a new modal dialog whatever it asks, so the dialog is mapped before it becomes modal.
The half-second timer now calls a new function that shows the window without asking for the focus, instead of present.
An open progress window is only un-minimized, because raising it gave it the focus when another window covered it.
No button is the default any more, and the job error message goes through the same code.
A new helper parks the focus on the text, shows the dialog, waits for it to appear, then runs it.
Enter typed elsewhere stays in your app, and Enter in the dialog does nothing until you pick a button.
Tabbing to Cancel, Escape, closing the dialog, and the buttons all work as before.
Under GNOME, an unfocused dialog may open behind your app, so you may need to click Thunar to answer.
To undo it, revert this PR. Nothing is saved anywhere.
The PR changes five Thunar source files and two headers, and adds the test and this page.
Part 2. How it was built and verified.
It was checked against the window manager spec, a small GTK test program, and Zorin's Thunar without the fix.
It builds, and the test program showed that xfwm4 focuses a modal dialog on map, but not one made modal later.
The verify script keeps another app focused through a long copy, three replace dialogs and an error, and its keys reach it.
Enter in the dialog does nothing, while Tab to Cancel, Escape and Replace still work.
On Zorin's Thunar without the fix, an earlier version of the same test fails: the dialog takes the focus.
All the sandbox tests pass with this build.
It wasn't run under GNOME, where the bug was seen; the sandbox has only xfwm4.
CI repeats the build and the test, and its screenshots are the proof to review.
A fresh review agent found two medium and three low findings; both medium ones and one low were fixed.
The dialog now waits for a real map before turning modal, and the error message no longer takes the focus.
The test now also copies a folder of thirty thousand empty files, to show the progress window without a question.
Two choices were kept: an open progress window isn't raised, and the permissions question follows the same rules.
CI's own review then reported ten findings, one of them medium, all handled in the next commit.
The wait for the map still ended too early, because Thunar runs no main GTK loop; it now waits properly.
The error dialog is titled Error, and the test was tidied; raising the progress window again was later taken back.
Three design points were kept, with reasons given on the page.
A second CI review confirmed the fixes and added a test where a second copy raises the open progress window.
Four more low findings were accepted, since none shows a failure in Thunar.
You chose to keep the dialogs modal once on screen, and the three earlier points, as they are.
A third review's test showed that raising a covered progress window gave it the focus, so the raise was taken out again.
Two more low findings about the test's timing and file count were accepted.
You chose to keep an open progress window from ever being raised.
A fourth review led to a test that retries with more files when the copy runs too fast, and two updated comments.
Four more low findings were accepted.
That also covers a progress window hidden behind another app when its job asks a question.
A review of the whole PR after merging main led to a clearer function name, a removed leftover, and one more error dialog.
Three more low findings were accepted.
You also chose to let the window manager restore a minimized progress window, rather than raise it.
After the merge, try a long copy while typing under GNOME, and run the split-view crash check.
Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue 14.
lines.say: Part 3. What comes later: nothing depends on issue fourteen.

lines.caption: Once this merges, only your own check in a real session remains.
In short: copying files no longer takes your keyboard, and a stray Enter can't cancel the copy.
